collection.credit:
* V9 "Age of Terrible Ideas": event prose, material applications,
  trial and consequence branches by ChatGPT. Core requests for intense
  conflict, fights, false guilt, courts, imprisonment, reconciliation,
  and the sixteen specific bizarre materials by Lorsieab2.

ledger.text: No actual game-role change unless supported by the patch.
ledger.why: designer note: the removal is story only

items.text: The healer writes 'NOT FOR PATIENTS' on the jar in huge letters.
The researcher offers the mixture to a builder for nonmedical testing.
The apprentice asks whether 'miracle cure' can be renamed 'miracle glue.'
A father holding a sleeping infant says, 'Please stop yelling about the slime. Some of us are trying to keep a baby asleep.'

intro.name: A miracle cure
intro.text: A talented but overconfident researcher has prepared an 'astonishing new remedy' containing {v9_materials} and {v9_materials.2}. A healer takes one look at the mixture and says, 'Absolutely not.'

question.name: Absolutely not
question.text: The researcher insists it is {a breakthrough|an ancient formula|a harmless demonstration|a triumph of science}. An apprentice admits (apprentice.he/she) has already labeled the jar 'MIRACLE CURE.'

text_only.reason: supplies go missing, not a villager

choices.label: Quarantine the mixture and inspect the notes.
Hold a public scientific demonstration with NO ingestion.
Ask the researcher to explain the evidence.
Investigate the suspicious disappearance of hospital supplies.

n1.text: The recipe was copied incorrectly from a pottery manual.

n2.text: The mixture was intended as wall pigment, not medicine.

n3.text: The researcher admits (researcher.he/she) was desperate for recognition.

n4.text: The apprentice altered the label as a joke and apologizes.

d1.text: The paste hardens around a wooden spoon. 'Useful,' says a builder. 'Not on a patient,' says the healer.

d2.text: The mixture foams spectacularly. The researcher cheers; the healer moves the audience farther away.

d3.text: Nothing happens. The researcher calls this 'remarkable stability.'

d4.text: The smell empties the demonstration area.

v1.text: The researcher cannot cite a single safe test. The claim is withdrawn.

v2.text: A child asks why something that smells awful must be medicine. The researcher admits it needn't be.

v3.text: A respected elder recognizes the substance as a traditional craft material and explains the misunderstanding.

m1.text: The apprentice moved the bandages to make room for the jars.

m2.text: A rival scientist hid a ledger, hoping to embarrass the researcher. The rival admits it and must repair the harm.

m3.text: The supplies are found on their proper shelf. Everyone looks at the inventory labels with renewed suspicion.

humbling.text: The researcher admits (researcher.he/she) wanted a discovery so badly that (researcher.he/she) ignored reasonable criticism. The healer says, 'You can try again. But not by gambling with someone else's health.'

disciplinary.text: The hospital holds a fair inquiry. The rival may receive a warning, restitution, or removal from a voluntary research assignment in the story.

text_only.reason: rule 7: an assignment is told only; the source says so (L4794)
